scenes.headline: A tour of the greeter module
scenes.subtitle: One small file, three exported functions
scenes.narration: This short video walks through the greeter module in the sample repository, what it exports, and how the command line entry point uses it.

scenes.heading: What the module offers
items: greet builds one greeting line for a single person
greetAll maps a list of names to a list of greetings
main reads names from the command line and prints them
scenes.narration: The module exports three functions. The first builds a greeting for one person. The second applies it to a whole list of names. The third is a small command line entry point that prints the results.
This function turns records into display rows. Each label is padded, upper-cased and clipped to one hundred columns, then a summary row reports the widest label, so no row ever exceeds the limit.
scenes.caption: The change pads the identifier and upper-cases the display name before pushing the row.

scenes.heading: Greeting a whole list
items: greetAll never mutates its input array
Each name goes through greet with default options
The result is a new array, one line per person
scenes.narration: For several people, greetAll maps over the array of names. It never mutates its input. Each name goes through greet with default options, so the result is a new array holding one plain greeting per person.

scenes.heading: The command line entry point
items: Arguments after the program name are treated as names
With no names, it greets the world with excitement
Otherwise it prints one line per name
scenes.narration: The main function skips the first two arguments, which are the runtime and the script path. Whatever remains is treated as a list of names. With no names at all, it greets the world with some excitement. Otherwise it prints one line per name.

scenes.heading: Why it is shaped this way
items: Pure functions are trivial to unit test
scenes.narration: The design keeps side effects at the edge. Greet and greetAll are pure functions, which makes them trivial to test. Only main touches the console. The exported interface documents the shape of the options object for every caller.

scenes.heading: Recap
items: main wires it to the terminal
scenes.narration: To recap, greet formats a greeting for one person, greetAll formats many of them at once, and main wires both to the terminal. That is the whole module, small enough to read in a couple of minutes.

scenes.headline: Small modules, clear edges
scenes.subtitle: Pure core, thin command line shell
scenes.narration: Thanks for watching. Small modules with a pure core and a thin shell are easy to read, easy to test, and easy to change when requirements move.
